cases.title: Trailing newline

cases.expected: Spec regexes use $ with re.search, so a final newline matches

cases.title: Non-ASCII digits
cases.when: the attack inputs run through pycall
cases.then: Spec regexes use \d and int(); Unicode digits match
cases.expected: Spec regexes use \d and int(); Unicode digits match

cases.title: Digit runs over 4300 characters
cases.when: the attack inputs run through pycall
cases.actual: parse raised ValueError from int() for run, round, part and attempt. A git ref component cannot reach 4300 characters. No spec limit applies.

cases.title: Long tails and backtracking

cases.then: No timing limit in the spec; record the cost
cases.expected: No timing limit in the spec; record the cost
cases.actual: Long slice and verify tails took 40 ms. A 100k-character tail of v0-a- repeated took 7.6 s (quadratic; 200k took 30 s). Seed for verify-limits.

seeds.title: parse accepts a branch with a final newline
seeds.detail: The row regexes end in $ and use re.search, so run-2 followed by a newline classifies as run and the tail keeps the newline. re.fullmatch or \Z would reject it. Git refs cannot hold a newline.

seeds.title: parse accepts non-ASCII digits
seeds.detail: \d matches Arabic-Indic and fullwidth digits and int() converts them: run-٣ gives n 3. The ASCII flag or [0-9] would reject them. Names then differ from names that name() builds.

seeds.title: parse raises ValueError on digit runs over 4300 characters
seeds.detail: int() hits the Python limit for run n, verify round and part, and attempt n. The CLI would print a traceback. A git ref cannot hold such a branch, so the risk is low.

seeds.title: verify row backtracks quadratically on long tails
seeds.detail: A tail of 100000 characters made of v0-a- repeated took 7.6 s. 200000 characters took 30 s. Send to verify-limits. The spec states no limit.

seeds.title: parse raises on non-string items in ids
seeds.detail: None or a list as an ids item raises AttributeError from .lower(). A bare string as ids iterates by character and gives known false. The spec says ids is an iterable of ledger ids.

seeds.title: verify id accepts NUL and any character
seeds.detail: Table row 6 uses (.+) for the id, so a verify tail with NUL gives an id with NUL. Other rows restrict the id.
